lens: Accessible interaction — keyboard-oriented use (simulated AI lens)
reason: The sampled public experience is coherent and readable in the supplied desktop/mobile hero captures. Its student-led consulting proposition, two audience actions, pending client-approval boundary and original-resume disclosure are clear. Source shows native station buttons, labeled form controls, associated application errors, visible focus treatments, 44px primary targets, native evaluation radios and a modal with cancellation focus restoration. I traced the client journey from services through contact submission and reviewed the corresponding passing mocked browser check. However, the operator discussion deck has a consequential keyboard collision and explicitly bypasses reduced-motion preferences. These prevent unqualified world-class agreement. This is an independent AI source/capture review, not observed user success or accessibility certification.

findings.evidence: Window onKeyDown excludes only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. Enter on a focused native button or Exit link also invokes reveal()/advance(). Buttons at lines 279-281 and 444-450 retain their native activation. reveal() sets drumroll and, after 1200ms, calls APPLY_STAGE_HASH (214-231) when eligible.
findings.userImpact: A keyboard operator activating sorting or Revisit can also initiate applying the displayed applicant result; Enter can advance a stamped card while activating another control. This is a source-established event collision, not a reproduced live incident.
findings.suggestedFix: Ignore events from interactive elements, modified keys, repeats and already-handled events in global shortcuts. Provide an explicit native reveal control. Add focused-button/link Enter checks that assert zero unintended result writes or navigation.

findings.evidence: Reduced-motion rules explicitly exclude .deck-root and all descendants. Deck styles retain 700ms fly/spin/swoosh entrances (522-531), looping shimmer/pulse, drumroll and shake. DeliberationDeck renders these classes (275, 312, 328, 348) and unconditionally waits 1200ms during reveal (218-219).
findings.userImpact: Motion-sensitive operators and projected-room viewers still receive sweeping, spinning and shaking effects despite requesting reduced motion. Public instrument reduced-motion tests do not cover this exception.
findings.suggestedFix: Honor reduced motion in the deck: remove spatial/decorative animations, retain immediate readable result/status changes, and skip the decorative reveal delay. Add deck-specific reduced-motion coverage.

notVerified: No keyboard-only end-to-end session, screen reader, zoom/reflow, forced-colors or full contrast/target audit was performed; screenshots cannot establish focus order or announcement behavior.
Supplied Chromium checks use clicks, synthetic application/operator fixtures and intercepted contact HTTP. Menu/dialog Escape focus checks are narrower than complete keyboard task acceptance.

No staging, hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration, authenticated live operator acceptance, physical-device, Safari/Firefox or human study evidence exists. Production readiness and real user success remain unproven.
